memory_update.text: VECO should be promoted as the primary US-listed underfollowed candidate for the compound-semiconductor photonics tools node because company disclosures explicitly connect InP laser manufacturing, silicon photonics, 800G/1.6T transceivers, hyperscale data centers, MOCVD, IBD and wet processing orders.

AXTI is a substrate-adjacent underfollowed candidate for InP/GaAs wafer exposure, but AI materiality remains unproven and needs revenue-mix, customer-qualification and capacity-utilization verification.

LITE and COHR should be used as demand/reference anchors for InP lasers, EMLs, CW lasers, silicon photonics, CPO and datacenter optical connectivity rather than as pure upstream tool bottleneck names.

Aixtron appears central to the global MOCVD/InP optoelectronics tool thesis in the provided external context, but it is not a US-exchange-listed candidate; evaluate separately in a non-US or ADR/OTC pass.

node: Compound semiconductor epitaxy and photonics manufacturing tools
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe for the compound-semiconductor photonics manufacturing node. The strongest underfollowed direct tool exposure found is Veeco, because recent company disclosures tie MOCVD, ion-beam deposition, wet processing, InP lasers, silicon photonics, 800G/1.6T transceivers, and hyperscale data centers into one order-flow chain. AXT is a less obvious wafer/substrate supplier and should be treated as a substrate-adjacent hypothesis until AI/datacenter materiality is verified. Lumentum and Coherent are higher-attention reference/customer/product-leader anchors: they validate demand for InP lasers, CW lasers, EMLs, silicon photonics and datacenter optical connectivity, but they are not the same upstream tool bottleneck.
